workforceModel.status: Digital and IT mature-team high-water model with a four-post permanent core, a rolling sandwich-year placement and unresolved specialist workforce sourcing
workforceModel.summary: The high-water funding model should not imply that every costed Digital and IT line becomes a permanent Student Hub post, but neither should it hide the enduring product capability that King’s is deliberately creating. The current planning assumption is a 4.0 FTE permanent Digital and IT core from the outset: Product Manager, Backend Engineer, Full-Stack Developer and UX/UI Designer. Mobilisation investment carries these posts to June 2029 and recurrent Digital and IT establishment takes over from July 2029, with the Product Manager cost allocation still to be agreed with the Staff Digital Hub. A rolling paid sandwich-year engineering placement is treated as a recurrent development and talent-pipeline commitment from BAU. Solution Architecture, DevOps, Dynamics, Cloud Infrastructure and IAM remain high-water specialist workforce capacity until Digital and IT confirms whether they are dedicated, shared or existing. Infuse QA is explicitly excluded from the workforce establishment because it is an outsourced non-pay testing service. Mark Peace as Product Owner and the expected existing IT Delivery Manager remain existing capacity rather than funded appointments.
